did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s title presents it as a song of thanksgiving by David after the Lord rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul.
Did you know? David uses a series of images to describe the Lord’s protection: rock, fortress, refuge, shield, horn of salvation, and stronghold.
Did you know? David describes his prayer in times of trouble as a prayer heard from the Lord’s temple, with his cry reaching His ears.
Did you know? The description of the Lord’s appearance begins with cosmic upheaval: the earth shakes and the foundations of the mountains tremble, expressing God’s overwhelming power.
Did you know? The psalm brings together several biblical storm images—arrows, lightning, hail, and fiery coals—to describe the Lord’s activity in the world.
Did you know? After describing the great storm, the psalm turns to personal deliverance: the Lord reaches out His hand and draws David out of deep waters.
Did you know? The phrase “He brought me out into a spacious place” contrasts trouble and danger with open space, symbolizing deliverance and freedom.
Did you know? David describes the strength the Lord gives him through two vivid images: running against a troop and leaping over a wall.
Did you know? The Lord is described as making David’s feet like the feet of a deer and setting him on high places—images of agility, stability, and the ability to face great heights.
Did you know? The psalm ends by extending thanksgiving beyond David himself to his dynasty: the Lord shows steadfast love to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
